introduction: NJ FamilyCare is New Jersey’s Medicaid and children’s coverage program. Apply through the FamilyCare pathway and review each applicant’s decision and plan-enrollment instructions.
description: NJ FamilyCare is New Jersey’s Medicaid and children’s coverage program. Apply through the FamilyCare pathway and review each applicant’s decision and plan-enrollment instructi

sections.who: Eligibility depends on category, household income, residence and status rules. Children under 19 can apply regardless of immigration status through Cover All Kids. Some adult non-citizen rules change in fall 2026; consult the current state update.
sections.get: Approved coverage helps pay for qualifying medical services. Coverage dates and plans depend on the individual decision; the provider portal is not the resident application route.

sections.apply:
1. Start the appropriate application

    Use Cover All Kids for a child or the linked NJ FamilyCare application. Call 800-701-0710 for help.

  2. Save the confirmation

    Keep the application copy and the eligibility agency contact listed on its confirmation page.

  3. Answer follow-up requests

    Provide requested records and read the result for each person, including health-plan selection.
sections.after: Keep contact details current. The state’s community-engagement update describes changes beginning in 2027 for certain adults; follow the notice for your coverage category and renewal timing.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Children’s application pathway, FamilyCare application checklist, Current federal-rule changes and timing. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Can a child apply without eligible adult immigration status?
Cover All Kids says children under 19 may apply regardless of their own immigration status, subject to other rules.
Must every household member have an SSN to apply?
The application checklist says you can still apply if an SSN is unavailable.
Are the new adult work rules already universal?
No. The state describes 2027 changes for particular adult coverage groups, with exclusions and individual notice.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
